Aida Overton Walker (1907) - an African-American vaudeville performer (dancer/choreographer)

Aida Overton Walker is arguably the most famous female black performer of the early 20th century. She is very well known for her 1912 performance of the “Salamone” dance at Hammerstein’s Victoria Theatre. This was her response to the national “Salamonia” craze of 1907 that spread through the white vaudeville circuit. Her portrayal of the Salamone character was very different from that of the white actresses of her time. Aware of how the roles she played had an impact on race relations of the time, she worked to break the stereotypes of black women as immoral and oversexed.
